title: Characterization of ZPP with Polynomial-Time Verifiers
statement: A language of bit strings belongs to the class defined by polynomial-time zero-error probabilistic machines if and only if there is a polynomial-time verifier and natural numbers $a,k$ such that, on each input $x$, the verifier uses $a(|x|+1)^k$ random bits, never outputs false on any random string when $x$ is in the language, and never outputs true on any random string when $x$ is outside it. On every input, the fraction of random strings for which it does not halt is at most $1/2$; polynomial-time efficiency means that the sets of encoded input-randomness pairs giving its true and false outputs both lie in $P$.
hypotheses_covered: $L$ is a language over bit strings
